issue.title: Edit and MultiEdit interEdit and MultiEdit interpret replacement text as JavaScript substitution patternspret replacement text as JavaScript substitution patterns

steps:
Create a file named split_lines.sh in the current directory with exactly the following content (keep every character as given):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# split_lines.sh: print every field of the first argument on its own line
IFS=,
read -r -a parts <<< "$1"
for p in "${parts[@]}"; do
  echo "[$p]"
done
In split_lines.sh, change only the line `IFS=,` to `IFS=$'\n'` so the fields are split on newlines instead of commas. Do not change any other line.
expected: Replacement text is stored literally, including dollar tokens.
defect: The Edit/MultiEdit tool modifies the requested replacement text while returning success.

fault location.explanation: String.replace uses replacement-pattern semantics instead of literal text.

Root cause: SOURCE-CONFIRMED. Non-replace_all edits use content.replace(oldString,newString), so JavaScript expands dollar replacement tokens. The archive reports all ten executions reached this defect, although one Judge submission failed and eight agents repaired the result later. Tool-level corruption and final-file corruption are distinct. Model: deepseek-chat, ACP with allow_once and sandbox disabled. The original steps are unchanged. No new agent replay or fixing-commit verification was performed; fixed_in remains unknown.
